title: SHCT — Slug–Hydrate Coupled-Transient solver

creators.name: Onyejekwe, Akosa Samuel
creators.affiliation: Cyprus University of Technology, Limassol, Cyprus

description:
A one-dimensional transient solver that carries the slug field and the hydrate field of a subsea multiphase pipeline in a single integration: holdup transport, conservative gas-mass continuity, an implicit pressure equation, energy transport and an advected hydrate phase field, closed by published correlations and a multicomponent Peng–Robinson flash, and advanced over a Monte-Carlo ensemble that returns a probabilistic time-to-plug.

v4.0.0 — the fluid model reported the liquid as the gas, and every number moved when it stopped. The flash returns y = z when a mixture does not split, so eos_properties handed back the FEED evaluated at its vapour root and called it the gas. On this live crude that is the liquid. 23 of the 49 nodes of the PVT grid have no vapour — every node at or above 150 bar — and all 23 reported 490–595 kg/m3 against a liquid of 975; across one grid interval at 100 bar the gas density stepped from 100.8 to 556.1 kg/m3 and the gas gravity from 0.65 to 1.76. The gas columns are now filled from the composition of the vapour the fluid actually releases on that isotherm, compressed to the node's own pressure and temperature. The gas at the critical sections is about eight times lighter than the solver had been using.

The momentum clip was setting the riser velocity, not bounding it. At the riser base 92 % of realisations sat exactly on the −2 m/s lower clip. Swept, the solution wants −5.5 m/s and is bit-identical at −10 and −20, with zero fallbacks and machine-precision mass error throughout, so the bound was inside the answer. It is now −10 and never binds: the clipped fraction of the velocity field is 0.000 on all three scenarios, against 0.022–0.025.

What the case study now reports. As-operated: subcooling 6.44 °C, peak ΦSH 0.339 against the derived Φcrit = 1.08, 0 % plug probability, 4.12 mm peak deposit, MEG 30.2 wt% over 20.1 km. The hazard remains the unplanned shut-in, which plugs 11 of 12 realisations at a P50 of 16.1 h with 34 % of the route above Φcrit over 23.3 km. The engineered fix removes the subcooling and buys a 65.9 h no-touch time at an effective U of 3.45 W/m2K — half what the previous release reported, because a much lighter gas is much less thermal mass to cool.

The drift-flux closure is now validated against 3-D CFD. The SHCT→OpenFOAM coupling had never been executed against an OpenFOAM install; running it (v2406) found seven defects in code that reads correctly, including an Allrun that exited 0 with every stage failed and a section-selection step that mapped a reversed flow onto a trickle forwards. It also showed the shipped comparison was circular: with the holdup imposed at the inlet, imposing 0.20 / 0.36 / 0.60 returned 0.2015 / 0.3637 / 0.5988. In a streamwise-periodic pipe, where development length does not exist, the distribution parameter measured directly off the field as <αgu>/(<αg><u>) converges over 34 passes to 1.146 against the closure's 1.172 — agreement to 2.3 %. On a developing segment the same quantity climbs 1.000 to 1.062 between 2.7 and 47 diameters without plateauing, which is what earlier developing-segment runs were measuring.

Consolidated deposit is no longer terminal by assumption. A cell is released when its own wall shear reaches the measured strength of consolidated hydrate (Di Lorenzo et al. 2018, 100–200 Pa), which is the condition sloughing was observed at. On this duty it changes nothing — the line sustains 66 Pa and peaks at 75 Pa — and that is checked rather than asserted.

Verification. 128 unit and regression tests, including one that runs real blockMesh, setFields and interFoam end to end where OpenFOAM is present. Well-posedness: the inviscid Kelvin–Helmholtz margin peaks at 1.96 and exceeds 1 over 4.3 % of the route, a short reach at the riser where the growth rate is grid-dependent.

What is still not established. Φcrit is derived and corroborated by a bifurcation it did not set, but it has not been MEASURED. C, n and kg0 remain unfitted. There is no whole-system comparison against a licensed transient multiphase code. The as-operated case is predicted to run above its own API RP 14E erosional limit at one station near the riser, which is an erosion finding before it is a hydrate one. Treat this as a hypothesis with a verified solver behind it, not a calibrated predictor.

Releases before v4.0.0 archive a fluid model that reported the liquid as the gas wherever the mixture was single-phase; their numbers are superseded. Cite this version or the concept DOI.
